newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Focus on engines after Indonesian plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Focus on engines after Indonesian plane crash.

text.p: The position of the propellors of an Indonesian airliner that crashed at the weekend killing 15 people indicated the two engines had stopped prior to the accident, aviation experts and news reports said on Monday.

The British Aerospace Advanced Turbo Prop (ATP) plane of Merpati Nusantara Airlines crashed into a coconut plantation while making its final descent to the Bulutumbang airport on Belitung, 400 km (250 miles) north of Jakarta, on an early morning scheduled service on Saturday.
There were 48 passengers and five crew on board.
"The only thing we can see from the photos at this time is that at least one engine was not operating at the time of impact," an aerospace expert, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.

Pictures published in Indonesian newspapers on Monday showed two propellor blades of one engine were undamaged. The expert said this showed the engine had been "feathered" or stopped and the propellor was not rotating at the time of the crash.
"Now the question is was the other engine operating and if two engines were not operating then we've certainly found the cause of the accident," the expert said.
The Kompas daily quoted a source close to the investigation as saying after examining both Pratt & Whitney engines that the propellors were found to be in the "feathered" position.
"This means both engines had stopped," the source said.
Aviation industry sources said the loss of two engines was normally caused by fuel starvation or by a highly unusual event like flying through a volcanic cloud or a thick hailstorm.

Airport authorities had said the weather had been fine and pilot had last contacted the control tower four minutes before the crash, saying the plane was at an altitude of 2,500 feet (800 metres) and ready to land.
Merpati said investigations were continuing into the crash with the cockpit voice recorder being analysed in Indonesia and the flight data recorder being sent overseas for analysis.
"The cause of the crash is not yet known as the investigation is still continuing," Merpati spokesman Tondo Widodo told Reuters, adding the cockpit voice recorder had not yet been analysed.
Widodo declined to speculate on the cause of the crash and whether the aircraft's engines had stopped.
"Until now we have not yet found any witnesses to the accident," he said.
Kompas quoted the Director General of Air Transport, Zainuddin Sikado, as saying all ATP aircraft operated by Merpati would be grounded until the cause of the crash was known.
